dossiers.bug: Control Center Now Playing module: tapping play/pause does pause or resume playback, but the module flickers (the whole card brightens, dims, a circle blinks, then it redraws again one or more times), the UI freezes for about half a second, and the play/pause glyph shows the old state. It corrects itself 1.5 to 3 s later at best. If the user taps again because nothing seemed to happen, the second toggle undoes the first.

root_causes.hypothesis: The icon is stale because the play state is read back once, about 430 ms after the key press, from a heuristic that needs about 1.5 s to notice a pause. The CC then writes that stale value into the shared npx state, and unlike every other player surface it has no optimistic override.
evidence: cc.inc.c:723-725: pc_toggle_or_replay(), then msleep(220) + msleep(130), then a single np_get() whose result is copied straight into npx under npx_mu. The read happens about 80 ms (pc_key hold, playctl.inc.c:76-85,88) + 350 ms after the key-down.
cc.inc.c:219-220: the glyph comes only from ni.playing in the npx snapshot (cc.inc.c:205). No local or forced state exists.
nowplaying.inc.c:373: playing = !stopped && pcm_open && !pcm_paused && now - pcm_last_ms < 1500.

hibymod_disp.c:803-810 and 826: pcm_paused is set only on SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_PAUSE and cleared on every write. docs/research_playback.md:48 and :58 verify that HiBy pauses by simply stopping writes ('0 writes to the PCM in 2 s'), so PAUSE is never seen and 'playing' stays 1 for 1.5 s after a pause. On resume, the decoder needs time to refill before the first write, so 'playing' can still read 0 at 430 ms.

nowplay.inc.c:8-29: the only correction is npx_thread, which polls every 1000 ms. The CC idle loop repaints on npx_changed only after a read_pkt timeout of 500 ms (cc.inc.c:673-675). Worst case, the correct glyph appears about 1.5 + 1.0 + 0.5 s after the tap, so users tap again and toggle back.

Other surfaces already work around this with an optimistic state: widgets.inc.c:109-111 (wg_np_force / wg_np_until), nowui.inc.c:805-806 and 1223 (nu.hold for 2500 ms), music.inc.c:1718 and books_ab.inc.c:2181 (playing = !playing). Only the CC lacks one.
Side case: with Bluetooth output, HiBy does not open /dev/snd/pcmC*p (hibymod_disp.c:834), so pcm_open stays 0 and the CC always shows the play triangle.

root_causes.hypothesis: The CC's own press handling causes the flicker. One tap produces 4-5 full-frame repaints with different module looks, separated by a blocking stall of about 0.5 s in the UI thread.
evidence: cc.inc.c:687: any touch-down on the module (hit==100) repaints with pressed=100. cc.inc.c:206 then draws the whole card at alpha 80 instead of 46, so the entire card flashes bright even for the play, prev or next buttons.
cc.inc.c:722: right after the finger lifts, another repaint returns the card to alpha 46 and adds the circle (cc.inc.c:218), so the card goes bright, then dim, then shows the circle.

cc.inc.c:723-724: pc_toggle_or_replay() runs synchronously in the UI thread. It calls np_get (shim plus a /proc readlink scan), pc_open_for (on first use it opens up to 16 /dev/input nodes O_RDWR and runs ioctls, playctl.inc.c:42-63) and an 80 ms nanosleep, followed by msleep(350). No frames are presented and touches queue up during this time, so the circle hangs and then vanishes abruptly.

cc.inc.c:726: a full re-render with the stale glyph. cc.inc.c:724 also sets npx_changed=1, so the idle loop at cc.inc.c:675 repaints the same frame again (cc_render + cc_mask_build + full present). About 1-2 s later npx_thread raises npx_changed once more and the glyph finally flips (cc.inc.c:675). The user sees the card blink several times.

cc.inc.c:195-201: every cc_render re-blends the status bar from the live fr1 (frames[1]). The HiBy pan hook overwrites frames[1] with no sequence lock (hibymod_disp.c:940), and HiBy repaints its top bar (play indicator) right after KEY_PLAYPAUSE. So the top 30 rows can change, or tear, on each of these repaints.

root_causes.hypothesis: HiBy's own repaint after KEY_PLAYPAUSE leaks through capture mode for single frames. The injected key reaches hiby_player, which redraws its play button, top bar and progress bar. If HiBy draws into the buffer currently being scanned and pans the same yoffset, its pixels are on the panel until the hook copies frames[0] back. Once playback runs, HiBy repaints continuously, so the flashes repeat. The volume-warning dialog flicker would come from the same mechanism.
evidence: playctl.inc.c:4-9 and 65-85: play/pause is a real evdev key written to 'jz adc keyboard'. Every reader, including hiby_player, reacts and repaints.

hibymod_disp.c:938-949: in capture mode the shell image is copied into HiBy's buffer only inside the FBIOPAN hook, so whatever HiBy drew into that buffer before the pan is not replaced until then. hibymod_disp.c:936 counts same_pans (pans to the already visible buffer), and hibyshell.c:1138 logs that counter when investigating the volume HUD. The author already suspected HiBy writing into the visible buffer.

hibymod_disp.c:966-969: after each pan, the previously shown buffer gets HiBy's frame back. This is only invisible if FBIOPAN returns after the scanout switch has latched (assumed in hibymod_disp.c:196-204 and docs/research_60fps.md:98).

handoff.md:44: the user sees the home screen flickering over an app with volume above 50, suspected to be the stock warning. Two recordings at 18-31 fps missed it, consistent with flashes lasting one frame.
hibyctl.c:426-432: fbrec exists precisely to catch one-frame writes into the visible buffer. It has not yet been run on this scenario.

root_causes.hypothesis: Replay-from-stopped path: when HiBy's queue has ended, the CC play button does not send a key. It sends an 'L' play-list request, which makes HiBy run its stock 'tap a song' sequence. That can change HiBy's view and track_id under the CC, so the cover is decoded again and the view is wrong after the CC closes.
evidence: playctl.inc.c:166-175: if np_get reports stopped && !playing, pc_list_send(&path,1,...) is used instead of pc_toggle.
docs/research_play_list.md:46,56: this is the same sequence as the UI's song tap.
nowplay.inc.c:20-27: a new track_id triggers np_cover (150-500 ms, spawns hibywall) and npx_changed, which means one more CC repaint (cover may blank or swap).
cc.inc.c:775: on close the CC does cmd('R') or launcher_present() without checking whether HiBy changed view meanwhile.

dossiers.compas_reference: CompasOS owns the audio engine, so its toggle is synchronous and reads authoritative state. In src/ui/player/transport/player_playback.c:243-291, toggle_play_pause() calls audio_toggle_pause(), then immediately bool now_playing = audio_is_playing(); set_play_button_state(now_playing). There is one repaint and no polling heuristic. ByOS cannot query HiBy's engine synchronously through the key path. The closest equivalents are (a) an optimistic flip with a hold timeout, as already done in ByOS widgets.inc.c:109-111 and nowui.inc.c:805, and (b) authoritative confirmation through the shim's 'Q' "pos" request, whose state field (0 pause / 1 playing / 2 stopped) is the same value the stock progress bar uses (playctl.inc.c:243-244, 341, 355-372). CompasOS also routes hardware and transport through its own state machine (src/hardware/input/hw_buttons.c, src/ui/application/gui_control_poll.c:370-378), never through injected key events. That supports keeping the CC's state machine local rather than inferring it from PCM activity.
fix_plan: 1. cc.inc.c: add an optimistic play state modeled on widgets.inc.c:111 and nowui.inc.c:805. Add static int cc_pp_force; static double cc_pp_until; and a helper cc_playing(const struct np_info *ni) { return now_ms() < cc_pp_until ? cc_pp_force : ni->playing; }. In cc_render (cc.inc.c:210 and 219), replace ni.playing with cc_playing(&ni). On npc==1 (cc.inc.c:723), before sending the key: take an npx_snapshot, set cc_pp_force = !cc_playing(&cur) and cc_pp_until = now_ms() + 3000. In the idle branch (cc.inc.c:675), clear the hold early once the snapshot's playing equals cc_pp_force (the same rule as nowui.inc.c:805).

2. cc.inc.c:724-725: delete the forced np_get() overwrite of npx and the npx_changed=1. That write pushes a stale 'playing' into the shared state that widgets and Now Playing also read, and causes a redundant repaint at cc.inc.c:675.

3. cc.inc.c:723: stop blocking the UI thread. Send the key from a detached thread, reusing the pattern of nowui.inc.c:172-176 (nu_key_thread) or widgets.inc.c:2002 (wg_pc_th), e.g. static void *cc_pc_th(void *a) calling pc_toggle_or_replay / pc_prev / pc_next. Optionally pre-warm pc_open_for(KEY_PLAYPAUSE/NEXTSONG/PREVIOUSSONG) in cc_prepare (cc.inc.c:473) so the first tap does not scan 16 evdev nodes.

4. cc.inc.c:687 and 720-726: give one consistent press feedback. Compute npc at touch-down (move the cc.inc.c:720 expression above line 687). When hit==100 && npc != 0, render with cc_np_pressed = npc and pressed = -1 instead of pressed=100, so only the button's circle appears and the whole card never brightens. On release, render once with cc_np_pressed=0 and the optimistic glyph. If a fade is wanted, animate the circle alpha over about 150 ms in a short frame loop that keeps polling read_pkt(…, 0), not msleep(220)/msleep(130).

5. nowplay.inc.c:8-29: confirm the real state quickly after a command. Add a volatile int npx_kick, set by the CC, Now Playing and widget toggles. While a kick is pending, npx_thread polls every 150-200 ms for 3 s instead of every 1000 ms, so the optimistic hold is confirmed or corrected well inside 3 s. Better still, while a kick is pending, ask the shim for authoritative state: in npx_thread call pc_position(&pos,&dur,&state) (blocking is fine in this thread, but pc_q is a single global and not thread-safe, so guard pc_q_* with a mutex or make the thread the only 'Q' user) and set i.playing = (state == 1).

6. hibymod_disp.c:803-826 and nowplaying.inc.c:373: make the shim heuristic faster. Record period_size/buffer_size in the HW_PARAMS branch (hibymod_disp.c:818-823) and in nowplaying.inc.c:373 use a threshold of max(300 ms, 2 x period duration) instead of a fixed 1500 ms. Optionally treat a SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_DROP/DRAIN with no write for more than one period as paused. This also fixes the 1.5 s lag in widgets, Music and Now Playing.

7. cc.inc.c:195-201: stop re-sampling the live fr1 status bar on every cc_render. Copy fr1's top 30 rows once in cc_prepare (cc.inc.c:496-503 already keeps sb_keep), and refresh that copy only in the idle repaint, reading frames[1] under a sequence check. The hook would need to bump a counter around hibymod_disp.c:940, e.g. reuse st->cap_frames: read it before and after the copy and retry if it changed. This prevents the top band from jumping or tearing on each tap.

8. hibymod_disp.c:921-970 (only if the step-3 fbrec recording shows HiBy pixels during CC toggles): log same_pans and cap_frames around the toggle. If same-buffer pans occur in capture mode, make the hook re-apply frames[0] to the visible buffer right after HiBy's same-yoffset pan: frame_edge(), then memcpy(buf_at(yoffset), frames, fsize). Or hold HiBy's presenter ('H' semantics) while the CC is open and release it on close. Shared fix with the volume-warning flicker.

9. playctl.inc.c:166-175 and cc.inc.c:723: for the replay-from-stopped case, keep the optimistic glyph. After the 'L' request completes (pc_list_poll), re-check HiBy's view before closing the CC: if HiBy navigated to its player, close the CC to the launcher with nav_start(NAV_HOME) just as cc_close_drag does (cc.inc.c:642-647), not cmd('R') blindly.

dossiers.bug: Playing a downloaded audiobook makes the screen glitch, cuts the audio briefly, and makes "the player close and reopen" before it plays normally. Path: Books > Audiobooks > book > Play. Code involved: ab_play() / ab_play_poll() / ab_open_player() in src/books_ab.inc.c, then the 'L' play-list command (pl_thread in src/hibymod_disp.c, inside hiby_player), then np_app_run() in src/nowui.inc.c, which is fed by the now-playing shim in src/nowplaying.inc.c.

root_causes.hypothesis: Most likely cause of the 'closes and reopens' effect: a UI state race, not a process restart. The Now Playing sheet opens about 0.6 s before the now-playing shim can see the new track. It first draws the PREVIOUS track as stopped (artwork shrunk to the paused size), with a hard cut and no entrance animation. When the track ID flips it does a full crossfade to the chapter with no cover. When the cover arrives (up to 1.5 s later) it rebuilds and crossfades again. Three full-screen changes in about 2 s look like the player closing and reopening, and it ends up 'already working'.
evidence: books_ab.inc.c:1734-1746 ab_play_poll() returns 2 ('open Now Playing') as soon as hiby_player answers rc=0, which is when play_index() returns, not when the new file is decoding.
books_ab.inc.c:2311-2312 ab_run: ch==2 -> ab_open_player() runs at once.

books_ab.inc.c:1879-1888 ab_open_player() calls np_app_run(under, -1, -1). With ix=-1 there is no zoom or slide-in: nowui.inc.c:1459 does nu_render(fr0) + present() as one hard full-frame cut over the Books page.

nowplaying.inc.c:352-365 np_from_shim only takes a file as the track once it has been open >600 ms. Before that it falls back to 'the last file read fully' with stopped=1, so nu_init (nowui.inc.c:664-667) snapshots the old track with playing=0. nu.sc is set to NU_PAUSE (0.80), so the art is drawn shrunk.

nowui.inc.c:790-800 nu_poll: when track_id changes it waits for the cover (cf) or 1.5 s, then calls nu_build_all() and returns -1. nowui.inc.c:1172 then runs nu_crossfade() (280 ms full-screen blend).

nowui.inc.c:826-833: when the cover appears for the same track_id (cov_ok changes), nu_build_all() runs again and returns -1, which is a second crossfade. Downloaded LibriVox chapters are not in the library (nu.alb<0, nowui.inc.c:646-647), so the art also goes through the 'nitida' background path (nowui.inc.c:823), which repaints the art band again.
The artwork spring from 0.80 to 1.0 (nowui.inc.c:1174-1176) adds a visible 'pop' once playing flips to 1.

root_causes.hypothesis: The audio cut and the extra glitch come from sending a new queue again. Every Play press rebuilds and restarts the whole list: list_tb_770x is rebuilt and play_index() runs, even when that same book or chapter is already playing. The main button always shows a Play glyph, so users press it on a playing book. If the player takes more than 5 s to answer (DB transaction on UBIFS plus SD I/O from the downloader), the shell gives up with 'the player did not respond'. A second tap then sends a second 'L', which causes a second cut and another full sheet sequence.
evidence: books_ab.inc.c:2205 H_MAIN: if ab_ndone, it calls ab_play(saved ch, saved pos) unconditionally. It never checks ab_np_ours() or whether this chapter is already playing.
books_ab.inc.c:2210 H_SEC on a downloaded chapter also calls ab_play() unconditionally.
books_ab.inc.c:1302-1305 the main button glyph is always Play (no pause state), which invites a re-press on a playing book.
books_ab.inc.c:1693 progress is saved only every 20 s or on a chapter change. Re-sending the list with p.pos therefore jumps back up to 20 s, so the user hears a cut plus a repeat.
books_ab.inc.c:1739-1741 hard 5 s timeout. After it, ab_play_id=0 and the late answer is discarded, so the sheet never opens and the next tap at line 2193 is allowed again.

hibymod_disp.c:1206-1265 pl_build holds the player's db_lock across BEGIN / DROP / CREATE / INSERT ... SELECT / COMMIT on /usr/data (UBIFS). hibymod_disp.c:1343-1346 notes UBIFS GC slowness. hibymod_disp.c:1374 then calls play_index(idx, pos, 0x10002), which stops the current decoder and opens the new SD file.
hibymod_disp.c:1386-1391 pl_kick ignores a second 'L' while busy, but PC_REQ has already been overwritten by the second rename (playctl.inc.c:150).

root_causes.hypothesis: A real hiby_player crash and restart caused by queue rows for 'unscanned' files. Audiobook chapters on SD/Audiobooks are not in MEDIA_TABLE, so they go into list_tb_770x with minimal data: id=-1-pos, format=0, sample_rate/bit_rate/size/end_time=0. Playing them, especially with pos>0, may crash the stock engine (bad decoder pick or divide-by-zero, SIGFPE on MIPS). The supervisor would then restart the player, which resumes the last list, so it 'reopens already working' and the display library briefly shows the player's own frames. The project docs say this mode was never verified on the device.
evidence: books_ab.inc.c:1720 pc_list_send_pos(..., 0 | PC_UNSCANNED, pos_ms): always unscanned, with a resume position.
hibymod_disp.c:1227-1237 with unscanned=1, rows go in as COALESCE(m.id,-1-r.pos), format 0, sample_rate 0, bit_rate 0, size 0, end_time 0.
docs/research_play_list.md:192 '[unscanned] inserted with minimal data (format=0). I don't know whether the player then derives the format from the extension [I]'.

root_causes.hypothesis: The memory guard and CPU contention make it worse. During an audiobook download, hibyabdl (a full hibyshell image) plus hibynet run next to the decoder starting up. The Books loop presents a full frame every 80 ms while the spinner and download rings animate. Under pressure, hibynet is SIGKILLed (downloads stall). After 40 s of severe pressure, hibyguard SIGKILLs the shell itself, because RSS is over 6 MB with the Now Playing buffers allocated. The screen then freezes on the last image and the shell restarts. Neither guard skips the moment a playback is starting.
evidence: books_ab.inc.c:2322-2325 anim covers ab_play_id, ab_nqueued and the playing book, so ab_present() runs every 80 ms (full ab_render + present) while the player is opening the file.

hibyshell.c:1643-1646 mem_watch SIGKILLs hibynet (when the radio is not active) below 4500 KB. hibyguard.c:186-191 does the same, and hibyguard.c:184 HELPERS does not list 'hibyabdl', so the downloader itself is never paused.

hibyguard.c:300-307 step 3: SIGKILL of hibyshell when severe for 40 s and RSS > SHELL_BIG_KB (6000). nu_init allocates bg/page/art/shadow (nowui.inc.c:661-662) on top of ab_open_player's lazy 300 KB 'under' (books_ab.inc.c:1882).
hibyshell.c:1698 rejuvenation (step 2) only happens at the launcher, so inside Books step 2 does nothing and step 3 is the only escalation.
hibymod_disp.c:1390 pl_kick creates a 512 KB-stack thread inside hiby_player (protected with oom -1000 by hibyguard.c:203) at the most memory-sensitive moment.

root_causes.hypothesis: Related bug that corrupts saved progress (so the next Play resumes at the wrong place and repeats the cut). play_index(pos) seeks right after open. The shim ignores seeks that happen less than 1.5 s after open, so position_ms counts from 0. ab_np_tick then saves that wrong position over the real one.
evidence: nowplaying.inc.c:378 'e->seek_ms - e->open_ms > 1500' drops the resume seek, so nowplaying.inc.c:386-388 gives position = frames since open.

books_ab.inc.c:1693-1699 saves pos when playing and more than 20 s have passed with |pos - saved| > 3000. ab_saved_pos is left at its old value by ab_play (books_ab.inc.c:1730 only sets ab_saved_ch), so the first save overwrites p.pos with the from-zero value.

dossiers.compas_reference: CompasOS does not drive the stock engine. It plays audiobooks through its own engine, and two of its design choices map to the hypotheses above. (1) Audiobooks go into the library scan: C:\Users\alber\AppData\Local\Temp\bo\ext\compas-player\src\library\metadata\scan\library_scan.c:145 (AUDIOBOOKS_LIBRARY_DIR_NAME is walked by the scanner). So it never plays rows with format, rate and duration unknown. That supports fix step 5: give the stock player real metadata instead of unscanned=1 rows. (2) Resuming inside long MP3 chapters uses a seek-point index built off the playback thread and cached on SD: src\audio\engine\audio_mp3_index.c:1-3, 41-67 (a scan-only decoder that never touches the live decoder), 83-84 and 328-345 (bounded retries so low memory cannot spin). It also notes that without a table dr_mp3 seeks by decoding from the first frame (src\audio\engine\audio_decoder_open.c:174-181). For ByOS this means a resume to pos=N minutes in a 64 kbps chapter can be expensive inside hiby_player. That is why fix steps 2 and 6 wait for the real track before opening the sheet and keep the downloader and UI quiet during that window.
fix_plan: 1. src/books_ab.inc.c, H_MAIN (line ~2205) and H_SEC (~2210): before calling ab_play(), call ab_np_tick(1). If ab_np_ours() and the playing directory equals ab_cur_dir: when the playing chapter is the one requested (ab_np_chapter()==ch, or for H_MAIN any chapter of this book), do not send a new list. Use pc_toggle() if paused, otherwise just ab_open_player(). Only send a list for a different book or chapter. In the button drawing (~1302-1305), show a pause glyph when this book is playing, the same way the minibar does (line 1020).

2. src/books_ab.inc.c ab_play_poll() (1734-1746): after rc>=0, do not return 2 at once. Store the target path (paths[idx]) in a new static ab_play_want[600] (set in ab_play) and enter a 'waiting for track' state. Return 2 only when np_get() reports !stopped && playing && path == ab_play_want, or after a 3 s fallback. Keep the 'Opening…' spinner meanwhile. Also raise the response timeout from 5000 to about 12000 ms. If a late answer arrives (pc_list_poll for the old id) after the timeout, accept it instead of discarding it (keep ab_play_id until the answer or 12 s).

3. src/books_ab.inc.c ab_open_player() (1879-1888): open the sheet with the slide-up animation instead of a hard cut. Add a mode to np_app_run (src/nowui.inc.c:1445), e.g. ix=-2 = 'rise from bottom', reusing nu_sheet_anim(H, 0, 0, 0.34f, 1, 0) from nowui.inc.c:682. Also seed the first frame. Add a small 'np hint' (title = book title / chapter, cover = <ab_cur_dir>/cover.jpg decoded to 128x128, playing=1) that nu_init (nowui.inc.c:658-670) uses when nu_snap gives a different or stopped path within 3 s of the hint. Then the sheet never shows the previous track or the paused-size art.

4. src/nowui.inc.c nu_poll (790-800 and 826-833): when the new track_id's path matches the hint and the hint cover is already shown, swap the metadata without nu_crossfade (return a band mask such as NB_PAGE|NB_ART instead of -1). Limit to one full crossfade per track (skip the second rebuild at 826-833 if the art source is already the book cover with the same checksum).

5. src/nowplaying.inc.c:378: accept a seek that happens shortly after open when it comes with our own pos= request. For example, set a shared 'expected start ms' (new field in hm_state, or pc_req_pos remembered in the shell) and anchor np_tr.anchor_pos to it when nseeks>0 && seek_ms-open_ms<=1500. In books_ab.inc.c ab_play (1729-1730), also set ab_saved_pos = pos_ms and ab_saved_t = now_ms(). In ab_np_tick (1693), do not save a pos smaller than the requested start during the first 10 s after ab_play.

6. Contention around the start (books_ab.inc.c ab_play): pause the downloader for the play window (kill(ab_worker_pid(), SIGSTOP), then SIGCONT once the track is confirmed or after 8 s). While ab_play_id is pending, present only the spinner band (present_rows) at at most 10 fps, not a full ab_present every 80 ms (books_ab.inc.c:2322-2325).

7. Unscanned rows (src/hibymod_disp.c pl_thread/pl_build 1227-1237, src/playctl.inc.c pc_list_write): verify on the device what the player does with format=0 / end_time=0 rows (see the reproduction steps). If that path is fragile, extend the request with per-file metadata (f=path, plus optional 'm=fmt|rate|bits|ch|dur_ms|bitrate|size' lines computed by the shell with hibytag) and insert those values in place of the zeros. Take the MP3 'format' code from a scanned MP3 row in MEDIA_TABLE (copy usrlocal_media.db and SELECT format FROM MEDIA_TABLE WHERE path LIKE '%.mp3' LIMIT 1). Alternatively, trigger the stock media scan for SD/Audiobooks once a download completes, so later plays are scanned rows.

8. src/hibyguard.c (184-191) and src/hibyshell.c mem_watch (1643-1646): add 'hibyabdl' as a level-1 'pause' target (SIGSTOP, then SIGCONT when calm) rather than letting only its hibynet child be killed. Make step 3 (hibyguard.c:300-307) skip SIGKILL while hm_state shows the shell inside a foreground app with a fresh heartbeat (it is busy, not leaking) unless memory is below SEV_KB for the whole window.

9. Logging to settle hypothesis 3 versus 1: in ab_play_poll / ab_open_player, log np path, stopped and playing at sheet open. In nu_poll, log each track_id switch with path and elapsed ms since open. Keep the existing 'pl:' lines in disp.log.
reproduce_on_device: Prerequisites: a LibriVox book fully downloaded in Books > Audiobooks with at least 2 chapters, and a different music track played from Music so the 'previous track' is not the book. Note `adb shell pidof hiby_player`, `cat /proc/uptime` and `ls /data/mnt/sd_0/hibymod/logs/`. Clear /tmp/hibymod/shell.log and /usr/data/hibymod/disp.log (copy them first).
Start high-fps capture: a phone camera at 240 fps on the panel is best (the panel scans at 44 Hz). Otherwise run a loop of `tools/hiby.py shot:f%03d` with no wait, though that is much coarser.
Case A (fresh start): Books > Audiobooks > tap the book > tap the main Play button once (H_MAIN). Do not touch anything for 5 s.

In the frames, look for: (1) the Books page with the 'Opening…' spinner; (2) a HARD cut (no slide-up) to Now Playing showing the PREVIOUS music track with shrunken (0.8) artwork and a play glyph; (3) a full-screen crossfade (~280 ms) to the chapter title with a grey/blurred or no cover; (4) a second crossfade or art-band repaint when the cover appears; (5) the artwork springing from 0.8 to 1.0. In the audio, listen for the music stopping and the chapter starting (and whether the chapter starts at 0:00 or at the saved position).

Right after, check `pidof hiby_player` and uptime. If the PID is unchanged and there is no new crash_*.txt in /data/mnt/sd_0/hibymod/logs, hypothesis 1 (UI race) explains 'closes and reopens'. If the PID changed or the uptime reset, hypothesis 3 (player crash on unscanned rows) is confirmed. Then read the crash report (signal 11 or 8) and disp.log 'pl: id=… rc=… ms=…'.

Pull /tmp/hibymod/shell.log and check the order and timestamps of 'audiolibro: reproducir … peticion N', 'audiolibro: respuesta rc=… filas=…', 'reproduciendo (suelto) en … ms', 'np: capas en … (caratula …, pista -1)', 'np: fundido de pista' (expected 1-2 times) and 'np: caratula nitida (sin biblioteca)'. Also check /tmp/hibymod/guard.log for 'step 1/2/3' lines and shell.log for 'memoria CRITICA'.

Case B (re-press): with the book chapter playing, close the sheet and tap the main Play button again. Expected bug: an audible cut, a jump back of up to 20 s, and the same glitch sequence. shell.log shows a second 'audiolibro: reproducir'.

Case C (slow answer): start a download of another book (so hibyabdl and hibynet are writing to SD), then tap Play on the downloaded book. Watch for the 'El reproductor no respondió' toast after 5 s, and check disp.log for 'pl: … ms=' above 5000 or 'pl: ocupado, orden 'L' ignorada' if you tap again.

Case D (resume position): play a chapter for 2 minutes, go home, wait for at least one 20 s save, reopen the book and tap Play. Compare the position the audio resumes at with where you left it. Repeat once more; with the bug, the saved position drifts back toward the time elapsed since the last open.
verify_after_fix: Case A at 240 fps: the Books page slides up into a Now Playing sheet that already shows the book cover and chapter title in its first frame. There is no frame with the previous track, no paused-size art, and at most one subtle band repaint (no full crossfade). Total time from tap to steady sheet should be under 1.5 s.
shell.log: exactly one 'audiolibro: reproducir' per tap and no 'np: fundido de pista' for the first track of the book. disp.log: one 'pl: id=… rc=0' line.
The hiby_player PID and uptime are unchanged across 10 consecutive plays of different chapters (fresh and resume), and there are no new crash_*.txt in SD hibymod/logs.
Case B: tapping Play on the book that is already playing only opens the sheet (or toggles pause). Audio is continuous with no jump back, and the button shows a pause glyph while playing.

Case C: with a download running, playback starts without the 'did not respond' toast. The downloader is SIGSTOPped during the start window (`cat /proc/$(pidof hibyabdl)/status | grep State` shows T) and resumes afterwards. Download progress continues.
Case D: resume lands within ±3 s of where listening stopped, across three resume cycles. The book.json/pos file holds the true position (not 'time since open').
Memory: /tmp/hibymod/guard.status during Case C shows no step 3 (shell kill), and 'memoria CRITICA' does not kill hibynet in the middle of the play start.

Regression: Music app album playback, Vinyl (freemusic, unscanned), Radio, and the Control Center play/pause still work. The Now Playing sheet opened from the minibar or gestures still animates as before (ix>=0 and the gesture paths are unchanged).

dossiers.bug: Cover art search often finds nothing, and editing the search text does not help: the grid stays empty, or it shows the same covers as before.

root_causes.hypothesis: The editor changes the query text but does not run a new search, and empty fields are rejected. In cover_search, the 'Buscar' button calls line_edit twice and only fetches again when both calls return true (lyrics.inc.c:190). line_edit edits the caller's buffer in place and returns e.len > 0 (keyboard.inc.c:1356, 1373). Cancel returns 0 without restoring the text (keyboard.inc.c:1378). So: (a) Cancel on the Album prompt, or after editing Artist, leaves new text in a/b. The header redraws it (lyrics.inc.c:182-183) but cover_fetch never runs, so the old or empty results stay under the new query. (b) Clearing Artist to search by album only makes line_edit return 0, so no search runs, and Artist is now empty for every later attempt. (c) The user is never told that no new search ran.
evidence: lyrics.inc.c:190 `if (line_edit(...Artista..., a) && line_edit(...Álbum..., b)) cover_fetch(a, b);`
keyboard.inc.c:1356 the ebuf points straight at the caller's buf, so edits are in place with no undo
keyboard.inc.c:1373 `return e.len > 0;` so an empty field counts as cancelled
keyboard.inc.c:1378 Cancel returns 0 and the buffer keeps the partial edit
lyrics.inc.c:182-183 the header label q is rebuilt from a/b every frame, so it shows text that was never searched
The lyrics screen has the same pattern (lyrics.inc.c:714), but there it searches Title/Artist and drops the album

root_causes.hypothesis: Stale thumbnails and JPEGs from an earlier search come back when a download in the new search fails. cover_fetch writes every candidate to the fixed paths NETDIR/c%d.jpg and c%d.thumb.raw and never deletes them first. It also reads the thumbnail without checking whether 'hibynet cover-get' succeeded: run_capture returns the byte count (>=0) even when hibynet exits with 1/2/4, and the exit status is discarded. When cover-get fails (CAA 404, timeout, image too large, progressive JPEG over 1600x1600, TLS failure on an archive.org redirect hop), slot i shows the cover from the previous search. Tapping it embeds the previous search's c%d.jpg. To the user this looks exactly like 'changing the search shows the same wrong covers'.
evidence: lyrics.inc.c:115-119 the thumbnail is read from NETDIR/c%d.thumb.raw no matter what cover-get returned
lyrics.inc.c:117 `if (run_capture(a2, o, sizeof o) < 0) continue;` only catches a spawn failure
tageditor.inc.c:31-45 run_capture waits on the child but never returns its WEXITSTATUS
lyrics.inc.c:200 saving uses NETDIR/c%d.jpg, which can be a file from an earlier search
hibynet.c:1165, 1175, 1186 cover-get returns E_NONE/E_NET/E_IO without deleting the earlier OUT.jpg or its thumbnail

root_causes.hypothesis: hibynet's artist filter is too strict and throws away valid iTunes hits. match_score sets g_art_miss=1 whenever the normalized wanted artist is empty, or when neither string is a substring of the other. cmd_covers then drops every such iTunes result (`if (g_art_miss) continue;`). Normalization only folds ASCII case and removes punctuation. Accents (Beyonce/Beyoncé), '&' vs 'and', 'The X' vs 'X, The', romanized vs native scripts, and 'Unknown' or folder-derived artists all count as misses. The artist sent is usually the library's album artist (music.inc.c:1450, 1468; nowui.inc.c:1146). That value is the HiBy DB album_artist, falling back to the track artist, and is 'Unknown' when the tag is missing (hibymix.c:603-625). For untagged albums the album title is the folder name (hibymix.c:625), e.g. 'CD1' or 'Downloads'. With an empty artist (only reachable from the tag editor, tageditor.inc.c:1118-1119), iTunes returns nothing by construction.
evidence: hibynet.c:872 `else { s += 30; g_art_miss = 1; }` also fires when a[0]==0, i.e. an empty artist
hibynet.c:925 `if (g_art_miss) continue; /* artista distinto */` drops every iTunes result
hibynet.c:855-863 norm(): ASCII lowercase only, no accent folding, no '&'/'and' or 'the' handling
hibymix.c:620 album 'Unknown' becomes '', then hibymix.c:625 sets album = folder name
hibytag.c:2479-2480 'Unknown' placeholder for a missing artist or album
nowui.inc.c:1146 passes ML->A[alb].artist (album artist), not the track artist

root_causes.hypothesis: The MusicBrainz/CAA fallback almost never matches noisy or partial queries. It builds an exact Lucene phrase query, releasegroup:"<album>" AND artist:"<artist>", and keeps only hits scoring 80 or more. Album tags with '(Deluxe Edition)', '[Remastered 2011]', 'Disc 1', '(CD2)' or a folder name, or an empty or 'Unknown' artist (which yields artist:""), score below 80 or return 0 or 400. Nothing strips edition or disc suffixes before either query, and the iTunes term is the raw 'artist album' string too.
evidence: hibynet.c:934 `releasegroup:"%s" AND artist:"%s"` with no cleaning except quotes and backslashes (hibynet.c:898-902)
hibynet.c:953 `if (atoi(sc_s) < 80 || !id[0]) continue;`
hibynet.c:911 iTunes term = raw `"%s %s"` of artist and album
hibynet.c:964-966 every CAA candidate needs another TLS HEAD to coverartarchive.org with follow=0 (307 accepted), which adds network time

root_causes.hypothesis: Network, TLS, rate-limit and timeout failures look like 'no covers found'. cover_fetch returns 0 when hibynet prints nothing, whatever the exit code: E_NET=2 (Wi-Fi down, DNS failure, TLS failure, missing cacert.pem), a kill by alarm(90), or an iTunes 403/429 rate limit (st not 200 and not <0, so it is counted as neither an error nor a result, hibynet.c:929). The UI always draws 'No se encontraron carátulas. Cambia la búsqueda…' (lyrics.inc.c:135), which tells the user to edit the query, and the edit fails the same way. getaddrinfo is not bounded by g_deadline, so slow DNS can run into the 90 s alarm, and SIGALRM kills hibynet with no output.
evidence: lyrics.inc.c:101 `if (run_capture(argv, out, sizeof out) <= 0) return 0;` discards the exit status
lyrics.inc.c:135 a single message for every failure
hibynet.c:929 and 970-971 a non-200 iTunes reply that is not <0 does not count as neterr
hibynet.c:1231 alarm(90) applies to the whole covers command
hibynet.c:216 getaddrinfo() runs outside the poll deadline
Lyrics already handles this correctly: lc_rc distinguishes 2 (network) from 1 (none) (lyrics.inc.c:282, 531)

root_causes.hypothesis: Local cover discovery is weaker than CompasOS, so albums that do have folder art show as 'no cover'. Once that happens, a negative-cache .none file is written. mu_cover_src only tries exact-case names (cover, folder, front, AlbumArt) in the track's own directory. It does not scan the directory case-insensitively, does not handle disc subfolders (CD1, Disc 2) by checking the parent or a sibling disc folder, and does not try album.jpg or .png in the oversize-embedded retry. A missed album gets <key>.none (music.inc.c:484, 502), which persists until the track or directory mtime changes.
evidence: music.inc.c:434-438 fixed name and extension list, exact case, own dir only
music.inc.c:491 retry list is .jpg only
music.inc.c:484 writes .none on a miss
CompasOS src/library/artwork/albumart/albumart.c:180 albumart_is_disc_folder(), :206-222 case-insensitive name ranking, :259-325 find_sibling_disc_art() (parent/sibling disc folders)

fix_plan: lyrics.inc.c cover_search (around line 189-191): edit into local copies (char na[128], nb[128] copied from a/b). Run a single editor, or call line_edit_suggest per field. Commit to a/b and call cover_fetch only when the user accepts. Restore the old text on Cancel. Allow empty fields: add a line_edit variant or flag that returns 1 for an accepted empty string instead of `e.len > 0` (keyboard.inc.c:1373). Search again when only one field changed. Apply the same fix to lyrics.inc.c:714, which also drops the album.

lyrics.inc.c cover_fetch (lines 112-120): before each cover-get, unlink NETDIR/c%d.jpg and c%d.thumb.raw. Use run_status (tageditor.inc.c:47), or a run_capture that returns WEXITSTATUS, and accept the thumbnail only when the exit code is 0. Better still, delete c0..c8 at the start of every cover_fetch and drop candidates whose download failed instead of showing a grey or stale tile.

lyrics.inc.c cover_fetch line 101: keep hibynet's exit code in a static cv_rc (0 ok, 1 none, 2 network, 99 missing binary or killed). cover_render line 135 then shows 'No se pudo conectar. Comprueba la Wi-Fi.' plus a Reintentar button for 2/99, as lyrics_render already does (lyrics.inc.c:531-532). Add EN/FR/ES strings.

hibynet.c match_score/norm (855-874): treat an empty want_art as 'unknown' (no penalty, g_art_miss=0). Treat 'unknown', 'various artists' and 'varios artistas' as empty. Fold common Latin-1/Latin Extended-A accents to ASCII in norm(). Remove a leading 'the ' and convert '&' to 'and' before comparing. Instead of `continue` on g_art_miss (hibynet.c:925), keep the hit with a +30 score so it is ranked below good hits but still listed when nothing better exists.

hibynet.c cmd_covers (904-983): add a clean_album() that strips trailing '(...)'/'[...]' groups containing deluxe|remaster|edition|expanded|anniversary|bonus|disc|cd, and trailing 'CD\d'/'Disc \d'. Use it for the iTunes term and the MB phrase. If the artist is empty, build the MB query as `releasegroup:"X"` without `AND artist:""` and the iTunes term from the album only. If iTunes and MB both return 0 hits, retry once with the cleaned album alone, then with a non-phrase MB query (`releasegroup:(X) AND artist:(Y)`), and lower the score floor to 60 for that pass.

hibynet.c: count iTunes HTTP 403/429/5xx as neterr (line 929), so rate limiting reports as 'network' rather than 'no covers'. Optionally pass an iTunes `country` parameter that matches the UI language.

Callers (music.inc.c:1450, 1468; nowui.inc.c:1146-1160): when the album artist is 'Unknown' or empty, pass the track artist. When the album title came from the folder name (hibymix.c:625; it could be exported as a flag in the 'A' row) or matches CD\d/Disc \d, pass the parent folder name or an empty album, so the first automatic search is meaningful.

music.inc.c mu_cover_src (406-441) and the retry (491): scan the directory once with readdir and strcasecmp against cover|folder|front|album|albumart with .jpg/.jpeg/.png. If the directory name matches a disc pattern, also check the parent directory and sibling disc folders, following CompasOS albumart.c:180-325. Keep the .none negative cache, but also delete <key>.none when cover_save succeeds.

docs/LYRICS_AND_COVERS.md and the header of lyrics.inc.c:7-9: lyrics.inc.c:8 says covers are saved as cover.jpg in the album folder, but cover_save only embeds (`(void)dir`, lyrics.inc.c:146). Make the comment and the docs match what the code does.

Music > Albums > long-press the tagged album (hold:X,Y,700) > 'Buscar carátula'. Expected with the bug: the progress card, then 'No se encontraron carátulas' or only 'caa' tiles. No iTunes tile appears even though iTunes has the album (artist filter, hibynet.c:925).

dossiers.compas_reference: CompasOS has no online cover search: no iTunes, MusicBrainz or CAA code under src/. Its useful reference is local art discovery, in C:\Users\alber\AppData\Local\Temp\bo\ext\compas-player\src\library\artwork\albumart\albumart.c. It checks folder.jpg/.jpeg/.png in order (lines ~146-167), ranks names case-insensitively with a single readdir pass (strcasecmp, lines ~206-222), detects disc subfolders with albumart_is_disc_folder() (line 180), and falls back to the album root and then to sibling disc folders with find_sibling_disc_art() (lines ~259-325). root_causes.hypothesis: The saved widget settings are thrown away when the shell restarts. When the shell starts twice in a row without staying up 25 s each time, self_heal() moves launcher.conf aside (renames it to launcher.conf.bad). lconf_load0() then finds no file and leaves the defaults compiled into widgets.inc.c: page on and the 9 default widgets. So 'page=0' and every widget the user removed come back, and the next lconf_save() writes those defaults to disk for good. The user's 'sudden closes' (shell crashes or restarts) and the test/deploy cycles running in the other chat (restart_shell.sh kills the shell and starts it again about 4 s later) fit this exactly. It also explains why the recent widgets_draw guard did not help: the flag is really 1 again.

root_causes.hypothesis: lconf_save() is not crash-safe. It writes launcher.conf.tmp with no ferror/fflush/fsync, ignores the fclose() result, renames over launcher.conf anyway, and never fsyncs the directory. Internal UBIFS storage is about 36 MB and nearly full. If space runs out partway through, or the device reboots or crashes hard right after a save, launcher.conf can end up cut short (stopping before the 'widgets' line) or rolled back to an older version. On the next boot the 'widgets page=0 ...' line is missing or old, so the page and the removed widgets come back.
evidence: launcher.inc.c:194-214 lconf_save: fopen/fprintf/fclose/rename with no error check and no fsync; the widgets line is written late in the file (launcher.inc.c:210, wg_conf_save at widgets.inc.c:72-77), after look/gestures/cc, so a short write drops it
by contrast wls_save (widgets.inc.c:189-194) checks fclose, starts_write fsyncs (hibyshell.c:1448), and mirror_save fsyncs (launcher.inc.c:910)
CompasOS saves durably: write, fflush, fsync, rename, then fsync the parent directory (compas-player/src/audio/effects/peq.c:887-965, peq_fsync_parent_dir)

root_causes.hypothesis: A stale home image published to HiBy can still show the widgets page. Three paths leave the launcher while the widgets page is on screen and publish that image without first returning to the normal home page: the Now Playing sheet, the Control Center's player page, and Music handing off to HiBy's library. home_shm then holds the widgets page. Turning the page off in Settings (apply_look) never calls home_publish(), and launcher_resume/launcher_present don't either. Every time HiBy's own home screen appears afterwards (for example closing Now Playing or a HiBy screen), hibymod_disp's home_substitute() puts that stale widgets image into HiBy's frame until the shell takes over. The user sees a flash of widgets even though the page is disabled. It persists until something calls launcher_leave()/launch_app().

root_causes.hypothesis: widgets_on is left stuck at 1 after leaving via those same three paths. launcher_enter_ex() and the home_hits instant entry set V.scroll = cur_page*W but do not clear widgets_on. dossiers.compas_reference: CompasOS saves settings so they survive crashes: it writes a temp file, checks ferror, then fflush+fsync, renames, and fsyncs the parent directory. If the rename fails it keeps a backup copy (C:\Users\alber\AppData\Local\Temp\bo\ext\compas-player\src\audio\effects\peq.c:887-965, peq_fsync_parent_dir / library_fsync_dir). It also writes its crash log with fsync (src/app/main.c:269-319). It never resets user settings because the app restarted; it only falls back to a backup copy when the main file is corrupt.

dossiers.bug: Most apps flicker, and apps sometimes close suddenly. The bridge has two writers. hiby_player's FBIOPAN hook and the shell's 'P'/'R'/'O' commands both write into the two /dev/fb0 pages. The shell publishes frames through a seqlock that the reader never re-checks, and the player frame (fr1) is read with no lock at all. Several restart paths (the library watchdog, hibyguard step 3, rejuvenation exec, and the new shell's immediate 'R') show HiBy's stock screen and can look like a crash.

root_causes.hypothesis: H1 (frames that lose the pill or popup, or tear). The fr0_shm seqlock only protects the writer. The library waits at most ~3 ms for an even sequence, copies anyway, and never checks the sequence again after copying. Each shell present also publishes 2-3 separate even states: the app frame, then the frame with the syspop card, then the frame with the volume pill. Whenever HiBy pans (it does so continuously while music plays) the hook can copy an intermediate or half-written frame. On screen the pill, the headphones card, the home bar or the status-bar tint disappear for one frame.
evidence: hibymod_disp.c:191-194 wait_even gives up after 300 x usleep(10) and the caller copies anyway
hibymod_disp.c:945-946 (capture pan hook): wait_even, then memcpy(b, frames) with no second sequence check
hibymod_disp.c:418-421 ('P'): same pattern, copy without a second check

hibyshell.c:181-189 present() makes fr0_shm even with the plain app frame (no pill or card), and only then hibyshell.c:190-191 calls syspop_after_present() and hud_after_present(), which each write the full frame again (odd then even): syspop.inc.c:38-41, hibyshell.c:1073-1076
hibyshell.c:1111 hud_after_present composes from fr0, not from the syspop result, so with the card and the pill both active the final frame has no card and the card blinks
hibyshell.c:183-185 statusbar_tint and homebar_layer modify fr0_shm in place after the memcpy, inside the odd window; when wait_even times out the library copies the untinted black bar

root_causes.hypothesis: H2 (HiBy content flashes over ByOS, and the high-volume warning flickers wildly with OK not tappable). During capture, HiBy sometimes pans the page that is already on screen (same_pans): it has drawn straight into the visible page, which holds the ByOS image. Its pixels are visible until the hook overwrites them. The hook then writes the shell frame into that visible page without first waiting for frame end (frame_edge), so the scan tears. A modal such as the high-volume warning redraws often, so it flashes on and off. On the ByOS home screen the main loop also bounces between launcher_leave and launcher_enter: (1) is_home(fr1) fails, so it leaves and sends 'R'; (2) a dialog frame that still matches the signature makes home_substitute paint the launcher over the dialog and bump home_hits; (3) that bump makes launcher_enter_ex(1) capture again. While launcher_on is set, touches go to launcher_touch, not to HiBy, so OK cannot be pressed.
evidence: hm_shared.h same_pans comment: 'dibujo directo en pantalla: lo que pinte se ve antes de que la libreria lo tape'

root_causes.hypothesis: H3 (status bar and HiBy-backed composites tear: broken Wi-Fi/percent, half-old frames in the sheet and HUD). frames[1] (fr1) has no lock at all. The pan hook memcpy's the new HiBy frame into it and then changes it in place (sb_fix memmove of the percent block, sb_bolt). The shell reads fr1 at any moment: status-bar composition, HUD compose, live Now Playing sheet animation, vs_overlay, OCR. A read during the hook's ~1-2 ms window gets rows mixed from two HiBy frames, or a percent block that is not yet shifted. That matches 'the Wi-Fi symbol breaks and gets bigger' when the percent block lands on top of the Wi-Fi icon.

root_causes.hypothesis: H4 (stale rows and top-band tearing after slow presents). 'P' writes the shell frame into the VISIBLE page right after frame_edge() and relies on the ~1 ms copy staying ahead of the 22.6 ms scan. Waiting on the mutex (HiBy's hook holds mu across its own blocking pan, up to 22 ms) plus up to 3 ms in wait_even plus preemption (the control thread is not RT) push the copy start late, so the top rows (status bar) show the previous frame. When the shell's 80/60 ms wait for the presents counter times out, 'P' bytes pile up in the FIFO. Each one bumps presents later, so the next present() returns at once and writes fr0_shm while the library is still copying. The shared dirty_y0/dirty_y1 is a single value that the next present overwrites, so a queued 'P' copies only the newest rows and rows from the earlier partial present stay stale on an idle HiBy.
evidence: hibymod_disp.c:415-424 'P': frame_edge(); wait_even; copies the dirty rows into buf_at(last_var.yoffset) (the visible page); presents++
hibymod_disp.c:196-206 comment: correctness depends on the copy outrunning the scan
hibymod_disp.c:921-922/960 HiBy's hook holds mu across r_ioctl(FBIOPAN), which blocks until vsync
hibyshell.c:193-194 present waits at most 80 ms on presents==p; hibyshell.c:1093/1103/1125 wait 60 ms; syspop.inc.c:55/94 wait 80 ms
hibyshell.c:107/187 present_rows sets st->dirty_y0/dirty_y1 for the NEXT 'P'; nothing accumulates them

root_causes.hypothesis: H5 (foreign or mixed content after release, and corner shimmer). The new 'restore' (giving HiBy back its raw last frame in the page that just went off screen) is applied only on capture pans. The 'R' release path and shell_release still hand HiBy a page that holds the sb_fix'd, bolted, corner-darkened frames[1], plus the overlay. HiBy then repaints only what changed on top, which reproduces the mixed status bar the restore was added to fix. Outside capture, sb_fix, sb_bolt, home_substitute, ov_apply and corners_apply all modify HiBy's own buffers in place on every pan. corners_apply is not idempotent: it multiplies the edge pixels again on every pan HiBy does not repaint, so the corners shimmer. The home_substitute pixels stay under HiBy's later partial repaints. Restore also assumes the page shown before is no longer scanned when r_ioctl returns. If the pan ever returns early (the 30-jiffy timeout path), restore writes HiBy's raw frame into the page still on screen and stock UI flashes for one frame.
evidence: hibymod_disp.c:949/966-969 restore runs only in the capture branch

hibymod_disp.c:349-372 corner_px scales by a/255 and is not idempotent; it also runs on every 'P'/'O' (422, 446) even for partial copies

root_causes.hypothesis: H6 (status-bar tint flickers inside apps). statusbar_tint uses row 31 of the frame as the per-column background, and a luminance threshold on row 31 to choose black or white icons. Any content that scrolls or animates under row 31 repaints the bar every frame. A partial present that starts between rows 1 and 30 leaves a mix of tinted and untinted rows, which drops the 'dark' count below 80 %, so the bar stays half black.
evidence: hibyshell.c:147-152 ref = d + 31*W, light = lum > 90; hibyshell.c:156 bg = ref[x] per column
hibyshell.c:185 tint is applied when dirty_y0 < 31, but only rows dirty_y0..dirty_y1 were re-copied from fr0; rows 0..dirty_y0-1 are already tinted, so the 'dark' test at :145-146 fails

root_causes.hypothesis: H7 (sudden closes that are really shell kills or restarts). (a) The library's watchdog SIGKILLs the shell after 10 s without shell_beat. Under memory pressure hibyguard keeps evicting program code from the page cache, so a long synchronous step on the shell's main thread (PNG mirror_save, decoding, a large redraw) can stall past 10 s. (b) hibyguard step 3 SIGKILLs the shell with no idle check, possibly in the middle of an app. (c) Steps 1 and 2 kill hibynet (network: covers, store, books) and hibybudsd (headphones), which also explains covers that are never found and Bluetooth that breaks. (d) Rejuvenation exec's the shell. (e) In every restart, the new shell sends 'R' (release) immediately, BEFORE it loads the config, wallpaper and icons and renders the launcher. HiBy's stock screen (or whatever HiBy was on, e.g. its player during an audiobook) is therefore shown for the whole load time, which is long under memory pressure, and the stock UI gets touches. That is the 'player closes and reopens already working' pattern.
evidence: hibymod_disp.c:620-633 watchdog: 10 s without a beat means kill(shell_pid, SIGKILL)
hibyguard.c:300-307 step 3: kill(sh, SIGKILL) when rss > 6000 KB after 40 s of severe pressure, with no foreground or idle check
hibyguard.c:184-191 and :288-298 kill_helpers: hibynet when oom_adj > -500 and hibybudsd at level 2
hibyshell.c:1696-1711 maybe_rejuvenate execv; hibyguard.c:297 rejuv_req
hibyshell.c:1790-1794 cmd('R') right after start, but lconf_load, load_wall, load_icons and render_launcher come only at hibyshell.c:1795-1817
