fix_plan: 1. hibymod_disp.c ioctl() capture branch (:938-949). Handle same-page pans. When shown_y == last_var.yoffset (HiBy drew into the visible page): copy that page into frames+fsize, write the shell frame into the OTHER page, and pan there with a modified copy of the arg. Do not write into the page being scanned. If you write into a page that is on screen, call frame_edge() first.

2. hibymod_disp.c 'P' (:415-424). Stop writing into the visible page. Copy frames (complete, never dirty rows only) into the hidden page, pan to it, then restore HiBy's raw frame (frames+fsize plus sb_raw) into the page that went off screen. This is the CompasOS pattern: write the hidden page, pan, then sync the other page. Update shown_y and last_var.yoffset the same way the hook does, so HiBy and the shell always agree on which page is front.

3. Seqlock reader validation (hibymod_disp.c: wait_even callers :418, :945). Read s1 = fr0_seq and copy only if s1 is even. After the copy, read the sequence again and retry up to 2 times if it changed. If it is still unstable, keep the previous on-screen frame and do not copy a torn one. Remove the silent 3 ms 'copy anyway' fallback.

4. One publish per present (hibyshell.c present() :169-196, syspop.inc.c:33-42/100-104, hibyshell.c:1062-1077/1107-1113). Compose the app frame, tint, home bar, syspop card and volume pill into one private staging buffer (reuse hud_tmp or sp_tmp). Write it to fr0_shm in a single odd-to-even window. Remove the separate seq++ writes in sp_present_over, hud_compose_present, hud_end and sp_finish, or route them all through one publish_frame(src, y0, y1) helper.

5. fr1 consistency (hibymod_disp.c :940-944). Run sb_fix and sb_bolt on a private 300 KB copy in the library (or only on the 30 status-bar rows, in a local buffer). Publish to frames+fsize under a new fr1_seq in hm_shared.h, appended at the end of the struct so older binaries keep working. In the shell, read fr1 through a snapshot helper with a sequence retry: at least rows 0-30 for compose_statusbar_on (launcher.inc.c:679), and the whole frame for hud_compose_present (hibyshell.c:1092) and compose_sheet live (hibyshell.c:719/758/851).

6. Present acknowledgment (hibyshell.c:193-194, hm_shared.h). Replace the 'presents changed' wait with a request ID: the shell writes st->present_req = ++n and the library sets st->present_done = n. Have the library merge dirty rows (union, min y0 / max y1, cleared on consume) instead of the single dirty_y0/y1. Have the library coalesce queued 'P' bytes, i.e. drain the FIFO and present once.

7. 'R' and shell_release (hibymod_disp.c:428-438, :533). Give HiBy back its raw frame (frames+fsize with sb_raw put back) in BOTH pages, the way restore does, and apply sb_fix, sb_bolt and corners only to the copy that is panned. For the non-capture path (:950-956), save the corner pixels and the percent block before changing them and put them back after the pan, as ov_restore does (or apply corners only when the frame hash changed), so repeated darkening and leftover content stop.

8. Volume warning and modal dialogs (hibyshell.c:1846-1857, hibymod_disp.c:162-177). Add a 'HiBy modal on screen' state: when on the launcher fr1 is not home and not vs_visible, leave and do not let home_hits re-enter for ~1.5 s, or until fr1 has matched home for 3 consecutive pans. Make home_substitute require 2 consecutive home-signature frames. While a HiBy modal is visible, forward touches to HiBy (hibyshell.c:1891). In vs_visible, also reject the high-volume warning layout.

9. statusbar_tint (hibyshell.c:142-168, :185). Before tinting, copy rows 0-30 again in full from fr0 (always, when the dirty range touches them). Take a single background colour from the app (the median of row 31, or an app-declared header colour cached per page) instead of per-column row-31 pixels. Add hysteresis to the light/dark decision.

10. Sudden closes. (a) hibyshell.c:1790-1794: on start, keep the inherited capture until the launcher is rendered (move the cmd('R') after render_launcher and present the launcher directly). Release only if the launcher is disabled. (b) hibyguard.c:300-307: before step 3, write rejuv_req and wait for the shell to be idle (add st->shell_idle to hm_state); SIGKILL only after a much longer grace. (c) hibyguard.c:184-191: do not kill hibybudsd while a headphone is connected or pairing, nor hibynet while a ByOS app in the foreground is using it (the shell sets oom_score_adj < -500 for both while in use, as it already does for radio). (d) hibymod_disp.c:629: raise the watchdog to 20-30 s and log the kill reason to a file (st->kill_reason). Log every restart cause to shell.log so device tests can tell a crash from a guard kill.
reproduce_on_device: Setup (only after the user allows device work): enable profiling with 'touch /tmp/hibymod/perf'. Start the uncommitted tester recorder (src/hibyctl.c fbrec, which polls the scanned page every 4 ms and catches writes into the visible buffer): adb forward tcp:5601 tcp:5601; adb shell "start-stop-daemon -S -b -x /usr/bin/hibyctl -- fbrec 5601 2 4000". Record from the PC. Also tail /tmp/hibymod/shell.log and the hibyguard log.

H1 (volume pill and card blink): play music so HiBy pans continuously. Open a ByOS app with an animation, e.g. Settings (tap its icon on home), then send key:106,event3 five times 120 ms apart. In the fbrec frames, look for frames during the pill fade-in where the pill at x 289-317, y 113-273 is missing for exactly one sample, or where rows 0-30 are pure black, not tinted. With headphones connected (buds popup on), the card at the bottom should blink when the pill is also active.

H2 (same-page pans and the volume warning): on the ByOS home screen, with headphones or a line out, hold key:106,event3 until HiBy's high-volume warning appears. In fbrec, look for alternating samples: launcher image, then HiBy dialog, then launcher, with a tear line in mid-frame. In shell.log, look for repeated 'el reproductor cambio de pantalla' / 'launcher fuera' / 'launcher activo (directo)' pairs every few hundred ms, and for a rising same_pans count in the 'volumen: tecla ... (pans al bufer visible: N)' lines. Tap OK at the dialog's position: it never reaches HiBy while launcher_on.

H3 (status bar): on home, with Wi-Fi connected and music playing (the percent changes and the clock ticks), record 60 s with fbrec. Look for samples where the percent block is drawn at its unshifted position or overlaps the Wi-Fi icon for one frame. Repeat inside the Music app.

H4 and H6: in Files or the Store, fling a long list. Look for samples where rows 0-~60 belong to the previous frame (tear band at the top), and for status-bar background colour changes that follow the content passing under row 31.

H5: open Control Center over a HiBy screen (e.g. HiBy's own Settings), close it, and look for a sample after the 'R' release where the status bar is mixed (percent shifted twice or Wi-Fi cut). Zoom on the corner pixels across 20 consecutive HiBy pans: their brightness should not keep changing.

H7 (sudden closes): keep free memory low (open Books, Vinyl and the Store in turn, then play a downloaded audiobook). Watch guard.log for 'step 3: shell ... restarted', shell.log for 'rejuvenecer', /tmp/hibymod/rejuv_count, and for a missing 'hibyshell activo' gap. In fbrec, look for HiBy's stock UI (player or mirror home) staying visible for longer than 1 s right after the shell restarts.
verify_after_fix: With fbrec at 4 ms over 5 min of mixed use (scrolling lists, the pill on top of animations, the CC music widget, the Now Playing sheet), zero samples contain a horizontal tear or mixed HiBy and ByOS content, and zero single-sample disappearances of the pill, card or home bar.
same_pans keeps increasing during the high-volume warning, but fbrec shows the dialog steady, with no on/off alternation, and tapping OK closes it. shell.log shows no launcher leave/enter loop.
The percent and Wi-Fi block is identical in every sample unless the battery value or the Wi-Fi state really changes. The status-bar tint stays one stable colour while a list scrolls underneath.
Corner pixels keep identical values across 100 HiBy pans with no repaint.
After 'R' from any ByOS screen, the next 10 HiBy frames show no status-bar artefacts.

Under the memory-pressure scenario: no 'step 3' kill while an app is in the foreground; no library watchdog kill (new kill_reason log stays empty); a rejuvenation shows the launcher with no stock-UI interval (fbrec gap less than one frame). The audiobook play path no longer shows HiBy's player before ByOS Now Playing.
perf lines in shell.log: the 'espera' (present wait) average does not grow (it should drop, because the 80 ms timeouts and the FIFO backlog are gone), and there is no frame with wait = 80 ms.
Check EN/FR/ES screens for the dialog and toast paths touched (no text changes expected).
dossiers.compas_reference: CompasOS (GPL) runs on the same R3 II 2025 with a single owner of the fb pages, and never writes to the page being scanned. lv_conf.h:236-275 explains the pan double buffering: render into the hidden half and flip with FBIOPAN_DISPLAY, because writing into the visible half tears. patches/lvgl/lvgl_fbdev_compositor.patch:511-536 (lv_linux_fbdev_present_ram_stage): memcpy into the target hidden page, then FBIOPAN, then commit yoffset only on success, then memcpy target into the other page ('keep both physical baselines coherent'). That matches ByOS's new restore step, but it covers every present, not only HiBy's capture pans. patches/lvgl/lvgl_fbdev_compositor.patch:568-580: while an external compositor owns presentation, all other flushes are dropped ('panning independently here ... would be an immediate tear/corruption risk'). That single-vsync-owner rule is what ByOS breaks, because HiBy's hook and the shell's 'P'/'O'/'R' both write pages. docs/research_60fps.md:243 in ByOS already recommends the same: 'A single owner of vsync during animations'.

topics.how_compas_does_it: CompasOS is GPL-3.0 (LICENSE at the root of C:\Users\alber\AppData\Local\Temp\bo\ext\compas-player). It also bundles third-party files under LGPL-2.1+ and GPL-2.0+ (for example src/audio/decoders/dst/dst_decoder.c:4 and src/audio/readers/sacd/sacd_reader.c:3), and its LVGL patches are under patches/lvgl/. ByOS ships under the 'ByOS Community License 1.0' (hibymod/LICENSE), a custom non-commercial licence that is not GPL-compatible. All paths in the other topics are relative to the compas-player root.
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: Do not copy any CompasOS code into ByOS: not functions, not comment blocks, not the LVGL patches. Doing so would make ByOS a derivative work under GPL-3 and would conflict with its non-commercial licence. Facts about the device are fine to reuse, because they are not copyrightable expression: file paths such as /usr/resource/config.json, /usr/bin/bt_enable and /usr/data/bluetooth, the BlueZ and bluealsa command sequences, thresholds, and the existence of a second dbus-daemon. Reimplement each approach clean-room from the descriptions in this report. Credit CompasOS as 'research reference' in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md or docs, but without bundling its code.

topics.topic: Bluetooth: daemon and bus health, adapter power on/off
topics.how_compas_does_it: (1) Split-brain D-Bus. /etc/init.d/S80_bt_init starts a second dbus-daemon (--config-file=/usr/share/dbus-1/system.conf) next to the S30dbus one. bluetoothd, bluealsa, bt-agent and the clients can end up on different buses. The symptom is incoming AVDTP being rejected with 'Authentication attempt without agent'. CompasOS counts dbus-daemon processes with ps. If there is more than one, or ListNames does not answer, it kills them all, removes /var/run/messagebus.pid and starts one 'dbus-daemon --system --fork' (src/network/bluetooth/control/bt_control_daemon.c:7-19, 143-154). (2) Adapter presence is checked by scanning /sys/class/bluetooth for hciN; it falls back to hciconfig and never waits about 15 s on 'bluetoothctl show' (bt_control_daemon.c:169-186). (3) Power state comes from an in-process D-Bus query, falling back to 'bluetoothctl show' (bt_control_daemon.c:268-322). (4) Wedged-bluetoothd recovery: 4 consecutive timeouts, or 'No default controller available' after a 15 s boot grace. Recovery is: single dbus, kill bluetoothd, 'hciconfig hci0 reset', '/usr/libexec/bluetooth/bluetoothd -E -C', then bt_enable and re-apply the bluealsa profile, with a 20 s cooldown (bt_control_daemon.c:199-245, 258-262). (5) Chip bring-up uses /usr/bin/bt_resume, not bt_init. bt_init spawns a duplicate dbus-daemon (bt_control_daemon.c:468-512). (6) Power on is /usr/bin/bt_enable (bt-adapter Powered On + Discoverable On). Power off is /usr/bin/bt_disable, never bt_suspend: bt_suspend tears down the UART link, and a later bt_resume fails until reboot (bt_control_daemon.c:534-590). (7) If hci0 is up but bluealsa was never started (hci0 restored without bt_resume), every connect fails with 'a2dp-sink profile connect failed: Protocol not available'. CompasOS therefore always ensures a bluealsa '-p a2dp-source' daemon is running (bt_control_daemon.c:395-456). (8) All chip and daemon operations are serialised by bt_chip_mutex and bt_daemon_respawn_mutex.
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: This is the most likely root cause of 'headphones never appear or pair' when stock HiBy works. ByOS's wireless.inc.c:15-17 drives BlueZ with 'dbus-send --system' and relies on HiBy's bt-agent. If S80_bt_init left two dbus-daemons, ByOS's dbus-send, bluetoothctl and HiBy's bt-agent can sit on a different bus from bluetoothd. Adopt these steps, off-device first: (a) add a diagnostic to the BT worker that logs 'ps | grep dbus-daemon' count, whether bluealsa runs and with which -p, and whether bt-agent runs; (b) check that /sys/class/bluetooth/hci0 exists and that 'bluetoothctl show' reports Powered: yes before scanning; (c) never call bt_init or bt_suspend; to toggle, go through HiBy's own setting as ByOS already does, or bt_enable/bt_disable; (d) before Pair/Connect, verify that a bluealsa a2dp-source daemon is alive ('bluealsactl list-pcms' or the process list); if it is missing, connect will fail with 'Protocol not available'; (e) add a bounded recovery with a cooldown only when the bus is clearly broken. Do not do this blindly while HiBy owns the stack: prefer logging first and confirm on-device with read-only commands.

topics.how_compas_does_it: Discovery runs inside a persistent 'bluetoothctl' child fed on stdin with 'scan.transport bredr' then 'scan on'. The client must stay alive while the scan runs. The default scan is 6 s, then 'scan off', 'quit', and terminate (src/network/bluetooth/control/bt_devices.c:225-259; ui/network/gui_network_bt.c:433-440). The list comes from 'bluetoothctl devices', with 'bluetoothctl info <mac>' per entry. Entries that are not paired and have no 'Class:' line are dropped. These are the LE-only identities of dual-mode headsets: they cannot carry A2DP and fail to pair (bt_devices.c:129-152). A refresh without inquiry ('list known devices') is used while audio streams, because inquiry makes A2DP stutter (bt_devices.c:261-267). bluetoothctl capability is probed once from '--help': 'paired-devices' (old) versus 'devices Paired' (BlueZ 5.87+), cached under a mutex (bt_devices.c:20-110). The connected state for the icon is answered with a single 'bluetoothctl devices Connected' call. A failed probe returns -1 ('keep the last state') rather than 'disconnected' (bt_devices.c:175-203).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: ByOS already does a BR/EDR-only scan through 'menu scan / transport bredr' (wireless.inc.c:532-537), which matches CompasOS. Add the following: (1) hide devices that are not paired and have no Class property, because those are LE twins of the same headset, and tapping them can never pair; (2) never show 'disconnected' or empty when a query merely fails, keep the last snapshot; (3) stop inquiry while A2DP is streaming, and use a known-devices refresh instead; (4) confirm on-device that 'menu scan' and 'transport' exist in HiBy's BlueZ 5.54 bluetoothctl; if they do not, the lines are silently ignored and LE floods return. Compare by watching 'bluetoothctl devices' output during a ByOS scan versus a stock HiBy scan.

topics.topic: Bluetooth: pairing agent, SSP, trust, connect order
topics.how_compas_does_it: CompasOS registers its own in-process org.bluez.Agent1 with capability DisplayYesNo on a private D-Bus connection, through RegisterAgent plus RequestDefaultAgent. It retries after a bluetoothd restart and kills HiBy's bt-agent once its own agent holds the default role. If its agent cannot register, it starts the stock 'bt-agent -c NoInputNoOutput -p /usr/data/pin.conf' instead (bt_pairing_agent.c:22, 551-598; bt_control_daemon.c:356-393). The agent only accepts calls from the current org.bluez owner (bt_pairing_agent.c:172-180). RequestConfirmation shows numeric comparison in the UI and replies later. RequestPinCode answers '0000'. RequestPasskey answers 0. AuthorizeService accepts only paired devices (bt_pairing_agent.c:197-296). Pairing is accepted only inside a 60 s window opened by the user's tap (gui_network_bt.c:45, 86; bt_pairing_prompt.c:49-55). While that window is open the adapter is re-made Discoverable at most once a minute, and DiscoverableTimeout (180 s in /etc/bluetooth/main.conf) is relied on (bt_pairing_agent.c:394-425). The connect flow (bt_devices.c:287-330) is: make sure bluealsa a2dp-source is up BEFORE pairing, because many headsets open A2DP right after bonding. If BlueZ no longer knows the MAC (BlueZ drops unpaired discovered devices shortly after a scan ends), re-scan BR/EDR for up to 12 s until 'info' sees it. Then 'bluetoothctl pair' with a 65 s timeout and the chip mutex released, then ensure bluealsa again, then 'trust', then 'connect'. An 'already paired' result counts as success.
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: ByOS calls Device1.Pair with a 40 s timeout, then Trusted=true, then Connect (wireless.inc.c:603-610), relying on HiBy's bt-agent. Fix these points in order of likely impact: (1) make sure the device still exists in BlueZ at the moment of Pair. ByOS stops its 'scan on' client, and BlueZ purges unpaired devices about 30 s after discovery stops, so Pair then fails with UnknownObject or 'Device does not exist'. Keep discovery running until Pair returns, or re-discover until Device1 reappears. (2) Check that a bt-agent is actually registered on the same bus as bluetoothd. Without an agent, SSP 'Just Works' and legacy PIN fail. If HiBy's bt-agent is not running (HiBy may only start it from its own BT screen), either start it the way bt_resume does, or register a minimal NoInputNoOutput agent in hibyshell. Clean-room: Agent1 methods returning '0000' or auto-confirm, plus RequestDefaultAgent. (3) Make sure bluealsa a2dp-source is running before Pair and before Connect. (4) Raise the Pair timeout to at least 60 s. (5) After Connect, write /data/bt_lastused.txt as ByOS already does, and let HiBy switch output.

topics.topic: Bluetooth: reconnect, link keys, trust persistence
topics.how_compas_does_it: Auto-reconnect is armed only on a confirmed power-off to power-on edge, with no DAC mode, and runs once per power cycle (ui/shell/gui_shell_bluetooth.c:297-330). A cancellable worker makes 3 attempts 2 s apart (network/bluetooth/reconnect/bluetooth_reconnect.c:49-80). bt_devices.c:404-525 describes what each attempt does. It only proceeds if the adapter is powered and no '/a2dpsrc/sink' PCM exists yet. It picks a target that is either the preferred MAC or the single paired device that meets all of: Paired: yes, Trusted: yes, not Blocked, and advertising the A2DP sink UUID (BT_A2DP_SINK_UUID, bt_devices.c:453-461). If more than one is eligible, it does nothing. It re-checks under the chip lock, ensures bluealsa, runs 'bluetoothctl --timeout 5 connect', then verifies with 'info'. On cancellation it disconnects. Bonds and link keys live in bluetoothd's StorageDir /usr/data/bluetooth (bt_rc_trust.c:17). A mgmt-socket watcher (HCI_CHANNEL_CONTROL, MGMT_EV_NEW_LINK_KEY) fingerprints new link keys, but only to bind Remote-Control trust to a specific bond, not for audio (bt_link_key_watch.c:17-80; bt_rc_trust.h:4-12).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: Rely on BlueZ's own bond store (/usr/data/bluetooth). Never delete or rewrite it, and use RemoveDevice only on an explicit 'Forget'. Always set Trusted=true after a successful pair, which ByOS already does; without it, reconnect from the headset side is refused. For auto-reconnect: trigger on the BT power-on edge, choose the device by bt_lastused.txt or the single Paired, Trusted, A2DP-sink device, use a bounded and cancellable connect with about 3 tries, and verify through bluealsa PCMs rather than only Device1.Connected. Do not compete with HiBy's own sys_server reconnect: check whether one is already in flight, for example a bluealsa PCM appearing, before issuing Connect.

topics.topic: Bluetooth: bluealsa output switching and audio-route truth
topics.how_compas_does_it: CompasOS owns its audio engine. It switches between three targets: LOCAL through tinyalsa, BT through a piped 'aplay -D bluealsa' or a rate-pinned PCM, and USB. It reopens only when requested_target differs from active_target, the same lazy check it uses for a rate change (src/audio/output/audio_output.c:44-82, 386-401). For BT it keeps a stable S24 pipe so that bluealsa is not reopened at track boundaries. It also prefers a rate-pinned PCM, because opening bluealsa at the track's own rate recreates the A2DP transport and drops the headset (audio_output.c:389-399). Whether BT audio is 'connected' is decided by 'bluealsactl list-pcms' containing '/a2dpsrc/sink', not by Device1.Connected (bt_control_daemon.c:338-343; bluetooth_control.h:104-118). A 'bluealsactl monitor' thread watches PCMAdded and PCMRemoved, applies codec, rate and soft-volume on a separate worker with a capped retry budget, and flags disconnects (bt_output_watch.c:1-60). Changing the profile (source versus sink/DAC) kills and respawns bluealsa with the full argument set, waiting at most 2 s for the old process to go and the new one to list PCMs (bt_control_daemon.c:670-779). A live link is never killed just to correct daemon arguments (bt_control_daemon.c:415-429).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: ByOS does not own audio: HiBy's player opens bluealsa. So ByOS must not restart bluealsa while it may hold a link. Use the presence of '/a2dpsrc/sink' in 'bluealsactl list-pcms' (or org.bluealsa PCM objects) as the single truth for the BT audio icon and the 'Connected' row. After Connect succeeds, notify the player the same way its own Control Center does (sys_server, bt_lastused) so that HiBy switches its output. If ByOS ever restarts bluealsa, only do it when no PCM exists, and pass the same arguments bt_resume uses.

topics.topic: Volume handling and volume UI (pill or popup)
topics.how_compas_does_it: Hardware keys go through a button-mapping layer. Repeated events are coalesced into one step with a count. Each step reads the current authoritative volume, not the slider, clamps it, applies it once, saves asynchronously, shows the popup and refreshes the top bar (src/ui/application/gui_screen_power.c:572-584). Slider drags are coalesced into at most 20 hardware writes per second (50 ms timer), with a final synchronous apply on release (src/ui/input/hw_volume_coalesce.c:5-49). The popup is built once on lv_layer_top and is only hidden or unhidden; it is never created or destroyed per press. Auto-hide after 1.5 s uses a single reusable timer, which is paused while a finger is on the slider. External echoes (BT or AVRCP, remote, keys) never write the slider while it is being dragged, which avoids knob snap-back (src/ui/player/transport/player_volume_popup.c:30-80, 109-182). Teardown deletes the timer so that a leaked timer cannot fight the new one (player_volume_popup.c:184-209). AVRCP volume changes from headphones reuse the same popup path (src/ui/application/gui_control_poll.c:135-140). The volume curve is a calibrated dB taper: -70 dB floor, exponent 0.53, 0.34 dB per hardware step. A max-volume cap is applied inside the clamp. Requests go through a generation-checked worker so that a stale drag sample cannot overwrite a newer value (src/audio/engine/audio_volume.c:39-140).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: For ByOS's own volume pill: build it once and only show or hide it; keep one hide timer reset per key; derive every step from the player's current volume (hm_shared state), not from the pill's last drawn value; coalesce key repeats (KEY_LEFT=105 / KEY_RIGHT=106 on event3) and drag samples to at most 20 writes per second, with a final exact write on release. Never redraw the pill from an echo while the user is dragging it. Redraw only the pill's rectangle and only when the value changes, so each key press costs one partial present, not a full-screen one. Test plan (off-device first, then hiby.py): single press, held repeat, fast up-down alternation, drag while keys are pressed, AVRCP change from headphones, pill timeout, and the pill shown over each app.

topics.how_compas_does_it: CompasOS has no modal EU dialog. It reads the stock threshold from /usr/resource/config.json: a flat JSON array, the entry with type="volume", vol_warn_enable != 0, and warn_vol[0].headset as the percentage (src/hardware/device/device_config.c:8-56). It uses that threshold in two places. (1) The top-bar volume digits turn red while volume >= threshold; -1 means the feature is off (src/ui/shell/gui_shell_topbar.c:477-501, 601-605). (2) A settings-registry rule: raising a SET_F_CONFIRM value such as max volume above the 'loud' threshold returns SETV_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED unless acknowledged. Lowering it never needs acknowledgement, and the default is 85 when the stock level is unknown (src/core/persistence/settings_registry.c:102-123; settings_registry.h:18-23; ui/settings/controls/gui_remote_settings.c:52-58).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: The flicker and the unpressable OK almost certainly come from two UIs fighting. HiBy's player draws its own warning dialog into its frames, while ByOS keeps presenting the shell image (capture mode) over them, so the dialog alternates with the shell on every pan. Taps also go to the shell, not to HiBy's dialog. Fix it in one of two ways. (A) Own the warning: read the same config.json threshold, and when the player's volume crosses it from below, show a ByOS-native confirm sheet. On OK, let the volume through; on cancel, clamp to threshold-1. Also stop HiBy's dialog from appearing, for example by clamping in the key path before HiBy sees the step, or by acknowledging it through the player's setting if one exists. (B) Detect HiBy's modal: frame-diff or an IPC hook. While it is up, release capture/held mode completely so HiBy's frames and touches pass through untouched until it closes. Either way, never present two sources on alternating pans. Add a test: key-up from threshold-2 to threshold+2 with hiby.py and a shot every 50 ms, then check that no alternating frames appear and that a tap on OK closes the dialog.

topics.how_compas_does_it: Wi-Fi: wpa_supplicant is queried over its control socket (STATUS, SIGNAL_POLL) with one 1.5 s deadline, non-blocking, falling back to wpa_cli (src/network/wifi/wifi_status.c:21-120). Signal levels map RSSI >= -50 to 3, >= -60 to 2, >= -70 to 1, else 0 (src/network/wifi/wifi_status.h:22-27). The query runs on a worker about every 5 s, at most one at a time. Each radio on/off change bumps a generation, so stale replies are discarded. A query that skipped the signal keeps the last level. The radio-off state hides the icon; enabled but not associated shows 'wifi_off'; connected shows one of 4 strength glyphs (src/ui/shell/gui_shell_wifi.c:55-158). Every Wi-Fi glyph (off and all strengths) is placed in one fixed envelope, NATIVE(0,28) BOUNDS(1,1,22,22) or BOUNDS(1,4,22,17), so the slot never changes size (src/ui/shell/gui_shell_topbar_layout.c:206-226). topbar_set_image() only sets the source and relayouts when the file actually changes, because lv_image_set_src invalidates even when the source is the same (src/ui/shell/gui_shell_topbar.c:350-359). Style setters are also write-on-change. Bluetooth: the icon is shown whenever the adapter is powered: 'bluetooth_off' when nothing is connected, 'bluetooth' when connected. It is hidden only when the radio is off. A separate A2DP icon and codec badge appear only when a '/a2dpsrc/sink' PCM exists. Both BT states share one envelope (gui_shell_bluetooth.c:303-390; gui_shell_topbar_layout.c:215-219). Optimistic state on toggle, and background results are ignored while a toggle is in flight (gui_shell_bluetooth.c:306-311, 570-588). Battery: 5 assets with thresholds 85/40/10 plus charging, a red recolor below 5%, per-digit labels rewritten only on change, and re-anchoring only when the measured width changes (gui_shell_topbar.c:420-474). Wi-Fi and BT slot order is stable: an icon that stays visible never moves slots (gui_shell_topbar_layout.c:596-626).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: For the Wi-Fi icon that 'cuts out and gets bigger': ByOS's own comment at hibymod_disp.c:961-966 says HiBy repaints only damaged parts onto a buffer that still holds the shell image, so its status bar mixes, and sb_fix/sb_bolt patch HiBy's pixels. Stop patching HiBy's status-bar pixels. Draw the whole status bar (rows 0-30) from ByOS's own state into a fixed-size cell per icon: same bounding box for every strength and for off; clear the cell to the bar background before drawing; draw only when (state, level) changes. Feed Wi-Fi from the wpa_supplicant ctrl socket on a worker with a deadline, discard stale results by generation, and keep the last level on a failed query instead of hiding the icon. For the missing Bluetooth icon: show it whenever the adapter is powered (the 'disconnected' glyph when no device is connected) and switch to 'connected' when a bluealsa PCM or Device1.Connected exists. Do not tie its visibility to a successful audio connect. Use the -50/-60/-70 RSSI thresholds.

topics.topic: Display: framebuffer double buffering, tearing, render cadence
topics.how_compas_does_it: CompasOS patches LVGL's fbdev driver. When yres_virtual >= 2*yres and line_length equals the packed stride, it hands LVGL the two mmap'd framebuffer halves as its DIRECT-mode draw buffers. LVGL always renders into the page that is not being scanned out, and flush_cb pans (FBIOPAN_DISPLAY) to it only on the last flush of a frame. bookkeeping (vinfo.yoffset) is only committed if the ioctl succeeds (patches/lvgl/lvgl_fbdev_compositor.patch:54-87, 824-927). LVGL's DIRECT mode re-syncs dirty areas between the two pages. After any external write it copies the presented page into the other page, 'so the next partial refresh cannot reveal pixels from before' (patch:531-533). An external-composition API lets the transition compositor own both pages for an animation: begin rejects nesting, flush_cb drops LVGL flushes while it is active, and end re-points LVGL's next target at the real inactive page (patch:200-226, 565-575, 695-733). A RAM stage renders the wake frame off-panel and copies plus pans it in one step (patch:743-771). The main loop renders once per pass, after all timers and worker results, with a cap of one render per refresh period. The pan blocks until vsync, so the loop locks onto the panel instead of a drifting 16 ms timer (src/app/main.c:895-950). Workers run at nice 10 or 19 so they never stretch a frame (src/core/process/worker_thread.h:12-40).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: ByOS writes into the currently visible page in several paths. buf_at(last_var.yoffset) is written after frame_edge() in the 'P', 'R' and 'O' handlers and in the touch-release path (hibymod_disp.c:196-205, 403-445, 533-536). This bets that a roughly 1 ms memcpy outruns the 22.6 ms scan at 44.3 Hz; any scheduling delay, or a mutex wait in wait_even(), produces a tear or a flash. Adopt the CompasOS model inside the bridge: (1) when the shell presents, write into the page that is not shown (yoffset ^ page), then FBIOPAN to it, and update shown_y only if the ioctl succeeds; (2) after a shell present, copy the shown page into the other page, so HiBy's next partial repaint starts from the same baseline and never reveals an older frame. This is the likely source of the 'flickers' and of the mixed status bar. (3) Give each present exactly one owner: while the shell owns the screen, HiBy's pans must not alternate content (one source per pan; drop or redirect HiBy's frames instead of interleaving them); (4) make the shell render at most once per vsync, after all state updates in that loop pass; (5) run Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cover and metadata workers at nice 10-19. These are ideas only: reimplement them in hibymod_disp.c without copying the patch.

topics.how_compas_does_it: Decodes are admitted against MemAvailable from /proc/meminfo (briefly cached), minus a per-priority reserve: player cover 2 MiB, visible thumbnails 4 MiB, background warmer 8 MiB. Size estimates account for the real peak of each decoder: JPEG workspace, PNG streaming rows plus the inflate dictionary, and the RGB565 output (src/library/artwork/coordinator/artwork_memory.c:12-112, 113-300). A failed or overflowed estimate is refused. A failure cache with mtime invalidation backs off 10 s on temporary failures and promotes a failure to permanent after 3 repeats, so a warmer cannot loop on an impossible decode (artwork_failure_cache.c:7-60). Once the screen has been off for a while, every rebuildable cache is dropped (thumbnails, lyrics, LVGL image cache, decoded images), keeping only the visible cover and the lock-screen art. RSS is logged before and after (src/ui/application/gui_screen_off_memory.c:12-50). The LVGL image cache is capped at 4 MiB (lv_conf.h:165-188). Risky parsers run in a short-lived child process with an RLIMIT_AS ceiling, are killed with SIGKILL on timeout, and a bounded set of unreapable children fails closed (src/library/metadata/isolation/metadata_isolation.c:25-60). Long-audiobook MP4 tables stay compact rather than expanded, because Linux overcommit lets malloc succeed and the first write then gets SIGKILL (src/audio/demux/mp4/mp4_demux.c:30-45). Embedded covers larger than EMBEDDED_COVER_MAX_BYTES are refused (metadata_xiph_mp4.c:253-258).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: ByOS's memory guard should become admission control: before any cover decode, image load or list build, check MemAvailable minus a reserve sized for HiBy's player (larger than CompasOS's, because HiBy runs alongside), and refuse rather than allocate. Overcommit means a failed check is the only safe warning. Add a negative cache keyed by path and mtime with backoff, and cap embedded-cover reads; multi-MB M4B covers are a prime OOM trigger. Drop all rebuildable shell caches on screen-off and when an app closes. Log RSS before and after so that guards can be verified from logs, without touching the device.

topics.how_compas_does_it: Audiobooks are a separate top-level 'Audiobooks' folder that the music scan skips (src/library/metadata/scan/library_walk.h:7-8; library_scan.c:145). The M4B/M4A demuxer stays compact for long files: stsz, stco and stsc are read through bounded 64Ki windows, and offsets are resolved on demand with a running cursor. Only files with at most 65536 samples get fully expanded tables (src/audio/demux/mp4/mp4_demux.c:30-45, 443-450). The moov cache is capped at 4 MiB (mp4_demux.c:740-746). Embedded M4B covers larger than the blob limit are skipped instead of malloc'd (src/library/metadata/parsing/metadata_xiph_mp4.c:253-258). Resume is deferred: the queue is restored with the play button showing paused and the progress display set to the saved position, clamped to the duration once the probe arrives. Decoding only starts when the user presses play (src/ui/player/queue/player_queue_resume.c:615-623; src/ui/player/screen/gui_player_metadata.c:693-699). The position is saved through audio_get_resume_position_seconds (src/ui/application/gui_control_poll.c:444). The Audiobooks UI itself is a plugin outside this repository.
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: The pattern 'press play on a downloaded audiobook, audio cuts, the player closes and reopens already working' matches HiBy's player being OOM-killed or crashing on open, then ByOS or the guard restarting it. Large M4B sample tables plus a multi-MB embedded cover decoded at the same time are the usual cause. In ByOS: (1) never decode an audiobook's embedded cover in the shell; use a pre-extracted, downscaled sidecar or a placeholder, and cap the embedded-art read size; (2) open at the saved position paused, then start playback with one command, rather than play, seek and replay; (3) do not send a second play or seek while the player is still opening the file (serialise through playctl); (4) check the guard and memory logs around the event to confirm whether it was an OOM kill or a guard restart before changing anything; (5) if the HiBy player itself cannot handle huge M4B files, show a warning or offer to split the file rather than crash.

topics.how_compas_does_it: This is a POSIX port of Rockbox albumart.c, local files only, with no online search (src/library/artwork/albumart/albumart.c:1). The order per directory is: '<album>.<ext>', then 'cover.<ext>', then 'folder.jpg/.jpeg/.png' (albumart.c:145-172). The album name is sanitised the Rockbox way: '"' becomes '\'', and characters such as * / : < > ? \ | become '_' (albumart.c:74-86). Folder-level art wins over per-track '<track>.<ext>' sidecars. After the track's folder it checks the generated cache, then the parent folder, then, if the folder is a disc folder ('CD1', 'Disc 2', ...), sibling disc folders sorted by name (albumart.c:174-300, 340-405). Embedded art comes from the tags. Generated caches are BMPs keyed by a hash, with stale detection by source mtime (albumart.c:490-530). An explicit 'Reload cover' action invalidates the cache and the failure cache for that album and its artists (albumart.c:1102-1150; ui/library/browse/gui_library_artist.c:1061). The failure cache is keyed by song id and source mtime (artwork_failure_cache.c:31-60).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: For 'covers are often not found, and changing the search text does not fix it': (1) before any online search, try the full local chain: embedded art, <album>.jpg, cover.jpg, folder.jpg/.jpeg/.png, the parent folder, and sibling 'CD n' or 'Disc n' folders, case-insensitively; (2) the negative cache must be keyed on the query, not only on the album. When the user edits the search text, the key must change, or that album's entry must be cleared, together with its 'not found' marker on disk and the in-memory failure state. Otherwise the old 'not found' result is served again, which matches the reported symptom. (3) Add an explicit 'Reload cover' action that wipes cache and negative entries for that album. (4) Use a short temporary backoff (seconds) for network and memory failures, and mark a failure permanent only after repeated hard misses, never after one timeout.

topics.topic: On-device testing, tracing and screenshot tooling
topics.how_compas_does_it: Screenshots mmap /dev/fb0 read-only and copy the visible region using var.yoffset and xoffset (the page actually being scanned), validating stride and bounds. Upside-down rotation is corrected, and the result is written as PNG through lodepng on a worker (src/core/system/lifecycle/screenshot.c:119-200). A hardware-button combo triggers it, and the remote-control HTTP server exposes /api/screenshot (src/network/remote/control/remote_control_state.c:242, 891-892). A frame tracer is armed by writing a command file on the SD card (compas_trace.command, with arm, stop and export) and reports status in compas_trace.status. It logs per-frame CSV: work, draw/flush, pan begin and end, pan failures, invalidated area, and handler and sleep time (src/ui/diagnostics/ui_frame_trace.c:19-28, 360-372, 455-470). A blit verifier compares what the panel shows against a fresh stock render after each optimised scroll blit, and dumps the first bad box (src/ui/diagnostics/ui_blit_verify.c:24-60, 131-240). Host-side unit tests (tests/*.sh plus *.c) cover parsers, the BT DAC route, cover-flow math and so on. scripts/tools/collect_device_info.py collects a read-only, redacted ADB report, scrubbing MACs, serials and mount paths (scripts/tools/collect_device_info.py:1-40). A BT debug option records an HCI snoop with btmon to the SD card for Wireshark (bluetooth_control.h:44-55; bt_debug_capture.c).
topics.what_byos_should_adopt: (1) Make tools/hiby.py 'shot' read the page at the current yoffset from FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO, as hibyshell.c:80-81 already does. Reading offset 0 or the wrong half shows the inactive page and fakes or hides flicker. (2) Add a frame-trace mode to hibymod_disp.c that logs, per pan, the timestamp, the yoffset, the source (HiBy or shell), whether the shell wrote into the visible page, and the time between pans. A flicker then shows up as alternating sources or as same-page writes in the log, without needing frame-by-frame photos. (3) Add a 'burst' mode to hiby.py (N shots at 20-50 ms intervals) for the volume-warning and Control Center widget cases. (4) For Bluetooth, capture btmon output to the SD card during a ByOS pair attempt and during a stock HiBy pair attempt, then diff them to see exactly where ByOS diverges (agent missing, device purged, Protocol not available). (5) Add a redacted collect-info script (MACs, SSIDs, IPs scrubbed, per the blur rule) to gather the dbus-daemon count, bluealsa args, bt-agent presence, and /usr/resource/config.json volume entry read-only.

gaps.notes: Read-only analysis; device not touched. Most important gap: the shell never reads st->vlog (written in src/hibymod_disp.c:686-696), so it cannot tell when a HiBy modal dialog (EU volume warning, USB mode, low battery, sleep timer) opens while a ByOS app owns the screen. That plausibly explains 'warning flickers and OK can't be pressed' and generalises to other HiBy dialogs (cases sys.hibydialog.*). Other code-evident risks: sb_fix battery-digit shifting interacting with the Wi-Fi icon (hibymod_disp.c:255-290) matches the 'Wi-Fi icon gets bigger' report; lang_sys_poll only relabels app names and lang_system falls back to Spanish (launcher.inc.c:220-226, i18n.inc.c:32-38). Uncovered areas: USB plug/storage/DAC/car mode, battery digit transitions and low battery, booting without SD and hot insert, external-app lifecycle and SD-installed apps, all 13 languages, midnight/time change, sleep-timer expiry, screen off/standby while overlays are up, shell rejuvenate exec and crash recovery, airplane persistence, OTA error paths, two overlays at once, rapid launches, gestures during cold load, SYN_DROPPED. Physical play/pause buttons (if the hardware has them) are not handled by the shell, which only reads KEY_LEFT/KEY_RIGHT (hibyshell.c:624,1841). I did not write a separate case for them.
